definitions.explanation: A situation of serious difficulty or suffering, often with no easy way out. Used for financial, personal, or organizational troubles.

examples.japanese: {苦境|くきょう}に{立|た}たされる。
examples.english: To be placed in a difficult situation.

examples.japanese: {会社|かいしゃ}は{経営|けいえい}の{苦境|くきょう}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}えた。
examples.english: The company overcame its financial difficulties.

examples.japanese: {長引|ながび}く{不況|ふきょう}で{多|おお}くの{中小企業|ちゅうしょうきぎょう}が{苦境|くきょう}に{陥|おちい}っている。
examples.english: Many small and medium-sized businesses are falling into difficult circumstances due to the prolonged recession.

notes:
A situation of hardship or adversity. Composed of {苦|く} (suffering/hardship) + {境|きょう} (situation/circumstances). Often used in news and business contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {苦境|くきょう}に{立|た}つ: to find oneself in a difficult position
- {苦境|くきょう}に{立|た}たされる: to be placed in a predicament
- {苦境|くきょう}に{陥|おちい}る: to fall into adversity
- {苦境|くきょう}を{乗|の}り{越|こ}える: to overcome adversity
- {苦境|くきょう}を{脱|だっ}する: to escape from a difficult situation
- {苦境|くきょう}に{追|お}い{込|こ}まれる: to be driven into a corner

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {窮地|きゅうち}: desperate situation, predicament — more urgent and critical than {苦境|くきょう}
- {逆境|ぎゃっきょう}: adversity — similar meaning but emphasizes unfavorable conditions one must fight against
- {困難|こんなん}: difficulty, hardship — more general; can be used as a な-adjective
- ピンチ: pinch, crisis — casual/colloquial equivalent
